title: France suffered the largest cyberattack in its telecommunications history
text:
ARGENTINA
France suffered the largest cyberattack in its telecommunications history
Telecommunications company Orange, one of the main service providers in Europe, suffered a massive cyberattack
French telecommunications giant Orange, one of the largest mobile operators in Europe and Africa, announced on Monday, July 28, that it had detected a massive cyberattack that affected its internal systems.
The company, which provides services to more than 290 million customers worldwide, including consumers, businesses, and institutional clients, reported that, as part of its response to the incident, disruptions were caused in most of its services, especially in France.
The attack was detected last Friday, July 25, and the company's cybersecurity subsidiary, Orange Cyberdefense, was activated immediately to contain and isolate potentially compromised services.
This intervention made it possible to limit the impact of the attack, but it also caused the interruption of numerous services and management platforms for corporate clients and consumers, mainly in French territory. Orange stated that the affected services would begin to gradually return to normal by the morning of Wednesday, July 30.
So far, the company assures that there are no indications that any customer data or the company's own data have been extracted. However, it declared that it remains on alert while the investigation continues. Orange also filed a formal complaint with the relevant authorities and refrained from disclosing further details about the attack for security reasons.
This incident occurs in a context of growing concern about cyber threats targeting the telecommunications sector in France. The National Agency for the Security of Information Systems (ANSSI) recently warned in its annual report about cyber espionage campaigns led by state actors.
The report documented multiple breaches in recent years, including unauthorized access to the core of mobile networks and satellite communications infrastructures, with the aim of intercepting communications of specific individuals.
Although Orange has not attributed the attack to any specific group, the nature of the incident shows similarities with other large-scale cyber campaigns attributed to the Chinese espionage group known as Salt Typhoon.
This group has been identified by the FBI and the U.S. CISA agency as responsible for recent attacks against telecommunications providers in the United States, including AT&T, Verizon, Charter, Lumen, among others, as well as in other countries. It has also been linked to intrusions in companies such as Comcast, Digital Realty, and the satellite communications company Viasat.
It is worth noting that this is not the first cybersecurity incident to affect Orange in 2024. In February, its subsidiary in Romania suffered an attack that compromised a non-critical application.
A threat actor who identified as ""Rey"" claimed to have stolen thousands of internal documents containing employee data, user records, source code, invoices, contracts, and up to 380,000 email addresses.
Orange, with 125,800 employees and revenues of 40.3 billion euros in 2024, provides telecommunications and IT infrastructure services through its Orange Business unit, and serves a diverse clientele in Europe, Africa, and the Middle East. It currently has 256 million mobile customers and 22 million fixed broadband customers.
